subsystems.name: Orbiter spacecraft bus
subsystems.role: carries the payload for years of cruise and a multi-year tour of the Uranus system.

subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: generates electricity where sunlight is roughly 1/400 as strong as at Earth.

subsystems.name: Remote-sensing payload
subsystems.role: images and spectra of the atmosphere, rings and moons.

subsystems.name: Fields and particles payload
subsystems.role: measures the tilted, offset magnetic field and the magnetosphere.

subsystems.name: Atmospheric probe
subsystems.role: descends into the atmosphere and measures composition before it is crushed.

subsystems.name: Communications and radio science
subsystems.role: sends data home and uses the radio link itself as an instrument.

buildSteps.title: Settle the science case and the design
buildSteps.detail: A decadal survey sets the priorities; concept studies then trade orbits and trajectories, which decide whether a Jupiter gravity assist is used and therefore when the mission can launch.

buildSteps.title: Build and qualify the instruments
buildSteps.detail: Each camera, spectrometer, magnetometer and detector is built, calibrated against reference targets and vibration-tested.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the orbiter
buildSteps.detail: The structure, tanks, thermal blankets and avionics are assembled around the instrument interfaces.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the probe
buildSteps.detail: A heat shield able to survive a very fast entry is laid up from ablative composite, the parachute is packed, and the science package and transmitter are fitted into a small pressure-tight body.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and test as one mission
buildSteps.detail: Orbiter and probe are stacked, then shaken, baked in a thermal vacuum chamber and checked for electromagnetic interference before the nuclear power units are installed at the launch site.

buildSteps.title: Launch and swing past Jupiter
buildSteps.detail: A heavy-lift rocket sends the spacecraft outward; a Jupiter flyby bends the trajectory toward Uranus, which is otherwise hard to reach without a very long cruise.

buildSteps.title: Cruise for roughly a decade
buildSteps.detail: The probe stays dormant while controllers run occasional trajectory corrections and instrument checkouts; radio signals take hours to travel each way.

buildSteps.title: Probe release, descent and orbit insertion
buildSteps.detail: Weeks before arrival the probe separates and coasts in, entering at high speed behind its heat shield, then parachuting and transmitting composition data while the orbiter listens and records it; the orbiter then fires its engine to be captured.

buildSteps.title: Orbital tour and data return
buildSteps.detail: The orbiter repeatedly flies past the moons, using their gravity to reshape its orbit, mapping the magnetic field, atmosphere, rings and icy satellites until power and propellant run out.

prerequisites.why: solar arrays are impractical so far from the Sun, and plutonium-238 supply is limited and slow to produce.
a few probes have descended into giant-planet atmospheres, but none at an ice giant, where entry conditions are poorly known.
hours of one-way light time mean the spacecraft must operate and stay safe without real-time control.
the mission must work after over a decade of cruise plus years in an unfamiliar magnetosphere.
only one spacecraft has flown past, so the magnetic field, radiation belts and atmosphere remain uncertain inputs to the design.

pathway.milestone: concept maturation and technology work on power sources, instruments and entry-probe designs
pathway.unlocks: a confirmed mission with a firm launch window.

pathway.milestone: launch using a Jupiter gravity assist
pathway.unlocks: the only relatively affordable trajectory to Uranus available for decades.

pathway.milestone: arrival — probe descent plus a multi-year orbital tour
pathway.unlocks: first in-situ measurements of an ice giant atmosphere and its primordial composition.

pathway.milestone: a comparable mission to Neptune, or a deeper Uranus atmospheric probe
pathway.unlocks: a genuine comparison between the two ice giants and their interiors, magnetic fields and moon systems.
